entry: Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol
note: A light face, from the light round of 2026-11, third batch: one small thing beside one sentence, not a walk up to a test. Made by the working session (a child) in Enrichment/light-round-2026-11/, where the makers and data stay; placed here by the Concierge. A challenger has now read this piece (2026-11-11); its verdict is in the section's challenge block. It was made before the challenge of the first forty came back (16 keep, 24 remake), so it likely carries the same kinds of fault that challenge found: a caption that reads more into the page than the page says, a 'what is real' line that owns too little, a count off by one where a parser was naive. Every section is a proposal until Loudon approves it.

pieces.title: The same card, twice
pieces.caption: The same message in two registers. The page's finding: “a four-card session that took ~60 seconds with jargon-laden text collapses to ~3 seconds when the surface speaks human and the steward's recommended option is one click away.” *What is real and what is a choice:* Every string on both cards is the page's, from its table of tone exemplars and its Origin section. The two layouts are mine and neither is a screenshot of the real page; the page does not say these exact strings sat on one card together. The amber and cyan are the page's words for the button and the pill, the shades are mine. The bars are 60 and 3, both approximate on the page.

challenge.by: challenger · light round, batch F (six sounds and four diagrams with numbers) · read-only dispatch

verdicts.file: Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol — rich — the same card, twice.svg
verdicts.why: Seeing the two registers side by side is worth having, and the honest line owns the mock-ups plainly. But the page already holds real pairs from the real session, and the invented protocol card is worse jargon than anything the page reports; and the leak names the wrong page.

remade.file: Speak Like a Person, Log Like a Protocol — rich — the same card, twice.svg
remade.what: Both cards were invented strings, worse jargon than the page reports, and they wore the Trickster entry's avatar, which is the wrong page. Both are rebuilt from the page's own table and Origin section, and the avatar and the leak are dropped.
remade.by: a dispatched workshop maker, a child, from the challenger's report; looked over by the working session; placed by the Concierge
remade.second_verdict: none: the remake has not been challenged again
